required_corrections: Keep the dahikat 'laughed vs. menstruated' ikhtilaf visible in the published copy (proposal flags it in risks — enforce it in the final piece); do not headline 'she laughs' as settled fact.

Reframe 'the laugh and the disbelief': incredulity ('woe to me... an old woman') is present in Hud 11:72 too. The clean, corpus-grounded contrast is between two physical GESTURES recorded across the two tellings (laughed vs. struck-her-face-in-a-cry), not joy-in-one-surah vs. disbelief-in-the-other. Avoid implying Hud lacks shock.

If the piece cites the صرر root's '6 verses', do not imply all six mean 'clamor' — 4 of 6 mean 'persist/be obstinate' and 1 means 'cold wind'; the clamor sense (صَرَّة) is in fact unique to 51:29. Either drop the count or state that the clamor sense itself is rare.
